author: Linnaeus, 1766
summary: 국내에서는 2018년 이후 봄(4~6월)에 제주, 울산, 경남 고성 등지의 논에서 몇 차례 기록된 길잃은새다. 얕은 물이나 젖은 땅에서 아래로 굽은 긴 부리로 진흙 속을 더듬어 곤충, 개구리, 작은 물고기, 고둥 따위를 잡는다. 남유럽과 아프리카, 중앙아시아·남아시아, 오스트레일리아, 아메리카 남동부 등지에 띄엄띄엄 분포한다.

art.subject: Glossy Ibis (Plegadis falcinellus), adult in breeding plumage, as seen in spring: head, neck, breast, belly and upper back deep chestnut-maroon; wings, scapulars and tail dark with a strong metallic green and purple gloss; bare lores dark, bordered by thin pale blue-white lines running from the bill base above and below the eye. Bill long, decurved, olive-brown to dark horn; iris dark brown; legs and feet dark olive-brown.
art.pose: wading in the shallow water of a flooded rice field, side view, the long decurved bill shown in full
art.scene: flooded Korean rice paddies in spring, shallow water reflecting the sky, levees with fresh grass; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view wading in shallow water: slim dark ibis with a small head on a thin neck, deep chestnut-maroon head, neck, breast and belly, wings and scapulars glossed metallic green and purple, dark bare lores bordered by thin pale blue lines above and below, long, evenly decurved brownish bill, long dark legs

adult breeding, in flight seen squarely from below: neck outstretched with the long decurved bill, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, dark chestnut body, uniformly dark glossy wings, short tail, legs trailing with the feet projecting beyond the tail
art.build: Medium-sized, slim, dark ibis, about the size of a Little Egret but with shorter legs, looking blackish at a distance. Small head on a thin neck. Bill one and a half to two times the head length, slender and curving downward evenly along its length. Legs fairly long and dark; the feet project beyond the tail in flight. In flight neck outstretched, rapid wingbeats alternating with glides, wings uniformly dark. Tail short and square.
avoid: Do not paint a bald black head and white body (Black-headed Ibis); the whole bird is dark chestnut with green gloss.
Do not paint it as a flat black bird; the body is rich chestnut-maroon and the wings are glossed green and purple.
Do not show a white-streaked head and neck on this spring bird; the streaking is non-breeding plumage.
Do not paint a red face or red legs (Crested Ibis).
